articles.title: ESPN ranks the WNBA's greatest players of all time; 6 UConn stars make the list
articles.summary: Two of ESPN's top three WNBA players ever starred at UConn; six former Huskies made the Top 30 list.
articles.body:
The WNBA's 30th season is coming to a close with a Finals matchup featuring plenty of UConn women's basketball representation, as four former Huskies play for the Golden State Valkyries.

To commemorate the occasion, ESPN released a list of the 30 greatest stars to ever play in the WNBA over the past three decades, also dotted with Geno Auriemma products. Here's a look at the six former UConn players on ESPN's list:

Over a glittering two-decade WNBA career, Diana Taurasi shattered the league's all-time scoring record by more than 2,000 points along with several other notable records: she's also first in scoring titles and playoff points, and tied for second in All-Star selections. For many years, this statistical dominance often made her a popular choice as the WNBA's greatest-ever player, but the recent rise of A'ja Wilson, who won her third consecutive MVP award this season, led ESPN to rank the Aces star at No. 1.

"Think of any basketball superlative and it applies to Taurasi," ESPN's Charlie Creme writes. "Tough. A winner. Clutch. Unrelenting. Brilliant as a shooter, passer and playmaker. She won big. She scored big. She played big. She has always been the player no one could take their eyes off of."

Moore squeezed a tremendous amount of winning into her relatively short eight-year playing career, winning four WNBA championships as she helped elevate the Minnesota Lynx into the league's gold standard under Cheryl Reeve. Her most statistically impressive season came in 2014, averaging nearly 24 points, eight rebounds and 3.4 assists en route to her only MVP award.

"Moore is the one player on this list for whom fans will forever ask, 'What if?' Her career was short by superstar standards," ESPN writes. "But those eight years before she stepped away to help fight for criminal justice reform were just so good."

Breanna Stewart is the only active UConn alum on ESPN's list and is still doing quite a bit to further her WNBA legacy after a decade in the league. The Liberty power forward finished fifth in MVP voting in 2026, adding to a decorated résumé that includes two MVP awards, eight All-Star appearances and three WNBA titles.

"With her 6-4 frame and 7-1 wingspan to go along with guard-level ball-handling skills and deep shooting range, Stewart might be the most physically distinctive player the WNBA has ever seen," ESPN writes. "She runs the floor brilliantly but can also lead a break. There isn't a position on the court she can't guard or an area of the game she can't influence."

Bird partnered with Taurasi for two seasons in UConn's backcourt before also heading west to start a career defined by longevity and loyalty. Across two decades with the Seattle Storm, Bird set all-time marks in career assists and games played that still hold up, resulting in 13 All-Star appearances, eight All-WNBA selections and four WNBA titles.

"It might seem unfair that Bird isn't in the top 10, but it reflects something in which point guards take pride: making everyone around them better," ESPN writes. "The player right ahead of Bird on this list, longtime Storm teammate Lauren Jackson, would attest to that. No one played more WNBA games or was more respected as a leader than the Seattle icon, who has a statue outside Climate Pledge Arena."

After a standout college tenure in Storrs, Tina Charles began a similarly accomplished WNBA career just down the road at Mohegan Sun Arena, earning two first-team All-WNBA selections and an MVP award over four seasons after the Connecticut Sun selected her No. 1 overall. Charles remained one of the WNBA's premier players across six more seasons with the New York Liberty, and in the twilight of her career, she bounced between several teams before returning to Connecticut and retiring with the Sun last season.

"A dominant force from the day she stepped onto a WNBA court, Charles was the epitome of reliability and productivity until her retirement in May," ESPN writes.

Cash enjoyed a tremendous, 15-year WNBA career primarily with the now-defunct Detroit Shock and the Seattle Storm, earning four All-Star appearances and three WNBA titles. She might still have a chance to build on her WNBA legacy a decade after retirement, with Cash considered an early contender to replace outgoing league commissioner Cathy Engelbert ahead of the 2027 season.

"Cash was never on the first team for All-WNBA or defense," ESPN writes. "Yet she is a player who could change games with her effort and energy, along with her talent."

articles.title: Caleb Wilson takes humbling lesson from getting crushed in NBA debut
articles.summary: On Wednesday, Caleb Wilson got his feet wet in his debut with the Chicago Bulls. However, the Bulls suffered a historic blowout loss to the Toronto Raptors,...
articles.body:
On Wednesday, Caleb Wilson got his feet wet in his debut with the Chicago Bulls . However, the Bulls suffered a historic blowout loss to the Toronto Raptors, 135-92.

Wilson finished the game with 16 points and 4 rebounds. But he also had 9 turnovers.

After the game, Wilson took it stride as a learning process, per Bulls on CHSN.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"I just feel like it's a learning lesson," Wilson said.

He also took responsibility for the turnovers, committed himself to correcting his mistakes, and looked ahead to the next game.

Wilson's maturity has already endeared him to those who expect nothing but the best from him. The No. 4 draft pick out of North Carolina has to shoulder the burden of carrying the Bulls from the doldrums of the NBA back to some semblance of legitimacy.

Undoubtedly, Wilson's ascendancy has become a focal point for an organization in the midst of a top-down rebuild.

He's already shown his potential preparation for his first season. In the NBA Summer League, Wilson made the All-Summer League First Team , averaging 23.5 points, 7.3 rebounds, and 2.5 blocks. In the preseason, Wilson was on top of his game . He averaged 15.8 points, 4.4 rebounds, and 2.8 assists per game.

Wilson's on-court talent, combined with his leadership, makes him a strong candidate for NBA Rookie of the Year.

The Bulls will travel to Milwaukee to play against the Bucks on Friday night. It was added to make way for Game 1 of the World Series. Then, they will play in their home opener against the Washington Wizards on Saturday night.

articles.title: How Zion Williamson ‘respectfully’ processed latest loss amid questions about Pelicans’ future with Jeremiah Fears
articles.summary: The New Orleans Pelicans have heard the promises before. New coach, renewed expectations, flashes of potential, and another opportunity to turn the corner. Z...
articles.body:
The New Orleans Pelicans have heard the promises before. New coach, renewed expectations, flashes of potential, and another opportunity to turn the corner. Zion Williamson has lived through enough of those cycles to know that optimism means little without results. A three-point, last-second opening night loss to Tyrese Haliburton's Indiana Pacers (123-120) was another frustrating reminder of how difficult it has been to translate talent into victories.

Williamson is not abandoning hope after one game under Jamahl Mosley . However, the two-time All-Star is no longer interested in pretending that being competitive is the same as becoming a contender.

"I can't even say…" Williamson told ClutchPoints before pivoting. "I feel like we are right there, like we are going to make that turn (under Mosley), but it's tough saying it when, respectfully, I feel like we've dealt with that in the past two to three years. And I've said it before, it's hard to win in this league. So if we want to win, (closing games) is a hurdle we've just got to get over."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

That carefully chosen "respectfully" revealed plenty about Williamson's mindset. He believes in Mosley's vision but understands the skepticism surrounding a franchise that has repeatedly struggled to turn promising performances into sustained success. The comments reflected both hope and realism about a core that has repeatedly hovered near the Play-In Tournament line in recent seasons only to fall short, leaving the franchise stuck in the NBA's purgatory of mediocrity cycle.

Rebuilding around the 'next' future is becoming an unignorable option with every loss.

Adapting to the NBA is rarely a smooth transition. Fears found out about the humiliation that comes with those very public growing pains firsthand in last year's season opener against Ja Morant. Williamson defended the then-rookie following a loss to the Memphis Grizzlies last October, and provided some new notes after losing to Tyrese Haliburton's Indiana Pacers to open up Year Two together.

Fears came back into this season ready to be the future, the face of the Pelicans going forward. Williamson will have the 20-year-old's back every step of the way.

"Oh yeah, (Fears) is going to stand his ground," Williamson smiled. "And I told him, 'as long as I'm out there with you, you're good man. Do whatever. Get in people's heads. Whatever it is, I'm going to be right there with you. I'm going to protect you.' So, that's just the energy he brings to the game and, not just to the game, that's who he is as a person. Like, he is a competitor who just wants to win. I've said it before, and I'll say it again that I'm glad he is with us."

Williamson's message after losing to Tyrese Haliburton was unmistakable. The Pelicans cannot keep celebrating how close they are to a corner. Eventually, they have to make the turn. If Fears and Missi are truly the future in New Orleans, the responsibility for making that future different begins with the veterans surrounding them today. And that bit of insight comes from the other All-Star on the team, Dejounte Murray.

articles.summary: The Oklahoma City Thunder (1-0) return home off an opening-night victory to host the Denver Nuggets on Thursday night in a matchup of Western Conference hope...
articles.body:
The Oklahoma City Thunder (1-0) return home off an opening-night victory to host the Denver Nuggets on Thursday night in a matchup of Western Conference hopefuls.

How to Watch Denver Nuggets vs Oklahoma City Thunder

Oklahoma City got 32 points from reigning two-time NBA MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and frustrated the San Antonio Spurs 116-104 in a Western Conference Finals rematch. The Thunder led by as much as 26 points and held off San Antonio down the stretch in a game that got chippy at times. Jared McCain came off the bench for 20 points, and Chet Holmgren finished with 14 points, seven rebounds, and four blocked shots while helping hold Victor Wembanyama to a career-worst 1-of-13 shooting night.

The Nuggets return three-time NBA MVP Nikola Jokić along with Jamal Murray and Aaron Gordon, but the supporting cast takes on a new look with the departures of Peyton Watson, Tim Hardaway Jr. and Bruce Brown. DeMar DeRozan signed with Denver after his release by the Sacramento Kings, and added EuroLeague Defensive Player of the Year Alpha Diallo, who went undrafted out of Providence in 2020 and spent two years in Greece before a four-year stint with AS Monaco.

The Thunder's NBA title defense ended in a seven-game loss to the Spurs in last year's Western Conference Finals, while Denver lost in six games to the Minnesota Timberwolves in the first round.

articles.title: Knicks superfans give baby ultimate name in honor of team's NBA championship win
articles.summary: The New York Knicks won their first NBA championship in 53 years.
articles.body:
This New York Knicks couple went above and beyond to celebrate the team's NBA championship win by naming their newborn son after the historic event.

When the Knicks clinched the title, Yvonne Gonzalez-Bradford was seven months pregnant, and she and her husband Vance Bradford already had names picked out for their bundle of joy. The couple decided on Lady Victoria if the baby was a girl, and Prestige Wisdom if the baby was a boy.

The city came alive after the Knicks won over the San Antonio Spurs in five games of the seven-game series, where there was nowhere in New York you couldn't hear ecstatic fans cheering, "Knicks in 5!"

Vance told Today.com that it sparked an idea to potentially change the name of their son as he asked his wife, "What if we give our son a name for a champion? What about Knickson?'"

Yvonne was on board, and Vance revealed that the name would be special not only to honor the Knicks winning the championship but because his family has been die-hard fans for years.

Two days later, Yvonne suggested Fyve as a middle name to reference the number of games that the Knicks won to bring home the title.

"You know how when something happens so well in your favor, you don't want to jinx it?" Vance says, recounting how excited he was to hear his wife's suggestion. "I was just like, 'Yep! Absolutely. That's it!'"

Vance added another layer to his son's name sharing, "The Roman numeral for five is 'V,' like my name, so he's named after me in a way. Five is also an indivisible number. So he's our indivisible champion. You can hear him cooing in the background right now."

Knickson Fyve was born on August 8, 2026, which is also significant to his mother, as he was welcomed into the world on Yvonne's birthday.

The couple has already been asked what will happen if Knickson decides to be a fan of another NBA team in the future.

"If he turns out to be a Celtics fan or a Sixers fan, again he's still Knickson Bradford, who is in the boardroom," Vance humorously says. "We wanted to have a very strong and firm name that would lead to a cool life. Knickson Fyve is definitely our motto. Knickson Fyve forever!"

The Knicks just finished their first regular-season game against the Philadelphia 76ers on Oct. 20. Before tip-off, the banner was raised to showcase their championship win as well as be awarded with their rings.

Unfortunately for the reigning NBA champions, they lost their home opener 100-106, but there is still more than enough time to get right back in rhythm.

The next game for the Knicks will be against the Boston Celtics on Friday, Oct. 23 at 7 p.m. ET.
